groceriesPerAdultEquivalent.basis: Average spending in Finland on food and drink at home, €362 a month per adult equivalent in 2024, priced here: prices are 1.00 times Finland's.
groceriesPerAdultEquivalent.limitations: Price levels from the 2021 international comparison, moved to 2024 with overall inflation; national prices, so the city itself may differ.

eatingOut.basis: Average spending in Finland on eating out and hotels, €196 a month per adult equivalent in 2024, priced here: prices are 1.00 times Finland's.
eatingOut.limitations: Price levels from the 2021 international comparison, moved to 2024 with overall inflation; national prices, so the city itself may differ.

1.basis: Electricity: 2,000 kWh a year (app assumption for 1 bedroom) at €0.2254 per kWh, the national household price with taxes.
1.limitations: Electricity use is an app assumption and varies with appliances, cooking and cooling.

2.limitations: Electricity use is an app assumption and varies with appliances, cooking and cooling.

3.limitations: Electricity use is an app assumption and varies with appliances, cooking and cooling.

4.limitations: Electricity use is an app assumption and varies with appliances, cooking and cooling.

waterPerPerson.basis: HSY water and wastewater fees for 2026 (€4.67 per m³ with VAT) at 130 litres a person a day; Motiva gives 90 to 270 litres, used for the range.
waterPerPerson.limitations: Landlords often bill water as a flat fee per resident, which can differ from metered cost.

transitPassAdult.basis: HSL 30-day season ticket, zones AB; the saver subscription costs €61.60.

healthcarePerPerson.basis: Household out-of-pocket health spending per inhabitant in Finland (€759.66 a year).
healthcarePerPerson.limitations: A national average across all ages; spending is lower for most working-age adults and higher for older people.

observation.basis: Municipal early-education fee from 1 August 2026: 10.7% of monthly gross household income above a threshold for the family size, at most €335 for the youngest child; under €32 nothing is charged. The second child pays 40% and each further child 20% of the youngest child's fee.
observation.limitations: Uses gross wage income only and counts children under 17 in the family size (the rule counts children under 18). Families of more than six use the threshold for six. Part-time care costs less.
